name: showreel-fc01-lookup-column

voice.text: Why does your lookup break when you add a column? V lookup counts columns: price is column two. Insert a column, and two becomes Color. Your total drops to zero. Use X lookup. Point at the price column itself. Now it follows the column wherever it moves.

caption:
Why does your lookup break when you add a column? 🧩

VLOOKUP counts columns. Its third argument is a number ("price is column 2"), so when someone inserts a column inside the table, column 2 is suddenly Color and every price turns into a word. SUM skips text, so your total quietly drops to 0.
Fix: =XLOOKUP(A6, $A$2:$A$4, $C$2:$C$4). It points at the Price column itself, so the range moves with the column, wherever it goes.
XLOOKUP works in Google Sheets and Excel 2021 / Microsoft 365. On older Excel, INDEX + MATCH does the same job.
Save it for the next time your lookup goes weird.
keywords: vlookup wrong value after inserting column

sources.note: VLOOKUP: col_index_num is the column number in table_array (first column = 1) that contains the return value
XLOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_array, return_array): exact match by default; Microsoft 365, Excel 2021 and later
Google Sheets VLOOKUP: index is the column number in the range, first column = 1
SUM: text in a referenced range is ignored
